scenario: Session Block Merkle root computed twice: once over all 4 entries, once with entry index 2 dropped
classification: Confirmed correct — not a new finding
note: Merkle roots differ as expected — closeSessionBlock() takes the entries array as-is and hashes each as a leaf, so a dropped entry produces a different tree deterministically. One open question worth flagging as SDB-GAR-04 (non-blocking, Type II gap): GAR-03 does not specify who is responsible for verifying a received Session Block's merkle_root against an independently-held copy of the entries — closeSessionBlock() itself has no verification counterpart (only construction). A verifySessionBlock(block, entries) function may be needed for a receiving party to detect this class of tampering, analogous to verifyChain() for the span-level chain.
